label: rejected
reviewer: blind fresh agent (renders + close-ups + gate report + rubric only)

evidence.V1: Front/3-4/silhouette read clearly as ring-headed staff, but the ring is only ~0.66 studs deep (top view shows it as a thin diagonal sliver), so from the side/edge-on the head collapses and it reads as a plain stick at 64 px
evidence.V2: Big (shaft + ring) and medium (collar knob, grip wrap, pommel) tiers exist, but the focal gem is the smallest element and leaves the ring interior mostly empty, so the head lacks a clear focal mass
evidence.V3: Shaft is a uniform untapered cylinder and the head a plain torus on a knob; oversized head gives some stylisation but the assembly still reads as stacked primitives
evidence.V4: Gem and collar carry chamfers that catch light, but thin gold grip bands read as flat unbevelled inlays and the spokes are raw octagonal prisms, so edge treatment is uneven
evidence.V5: No seams, patches or z-fighting; gates A17/A18 clean (0 self-intersections, 0 cap overlaps, 0 flipped), but ring_studio close-up shows a visibly segmented polygonal torus contour and the grip bulges step along the outline (stray faceting)
evidence.V6: Disciplined: gold accent plus one hue in three values (dark shaft, mid grip, light gem); colourways (crimson, shadow) keep the same structure cleanly
evidence.V7: 1952 tris vs weapon target 2500 / ceiling 4000: under target
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, gold accent + single hue in 3 values, smooth shading, chamfers visible on gem/collar at kit-like scale
evidence.V9: Studio line: Tool Handle, origin at grip, Hull collision, CanCollide off when equipped, Massless, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic

artifacts: Ring torus has too few segments: polygonal stepping along its outer/inner contour in the ring_studio close-up
Grip wrap bulges show faceted stepping on the silhouette edge
Spokes are visibly octagonal prisms at close range
83 cross-shell overlaps (intentional interpenetration of parts; allowed, not visible)
top_fixes: Make the head read edge-on: thicken the ring depth or add a perpendicular second ring/side ornaments so the side and top silhouettes keep the staff's identity
Enlarge the gem to fill ~40-50% of the ring interior (or add a secondary motif) so the focal point dominates the head
Raise torus major/minor segment counts (and grip bulge segments) to remove contour faceting
Give the shaft a taper or mid-shaft ornament to push stylised proportion beyond a uniform cylinder
Chamfer the gold grip bands and spoke ends to match the ~0.045 stud kit bevel so edges catch light consistently
